etymology: Blend of "deposition" + "de-position" - the move of taking a witness out of their position, one objection at a time.
trigger: A deposition where the witness's account is the thing that would settle it, and the clock belongs to the side that talks.
tell: The objections are spoken, not reserved: form, foundation, asked and answered, vague - each one a pause, each pause a page, and the instruction not to answer arrives before the answer does.
counter: Object in one word and let the answer land on the record: objection, form, then the answer, then a ruling at the end. The derailment needs the objection to be a speech, and no rule requires a speech.

confused_with.tell: The sealion will not accept an answer and keeps asking; the depositioning will not allow an answer and keeps objecting.
The heckler's veto stops the room; the depositioning stops the record, and the room goes on looking orderly.

senses: The move of derailing a deposition from inside the format: speaking objections, instructions not to answer, a break every twenty minutes, so that six hours of testimony produce a transcript with nothing in it that can be read out.
It works because the record is the product, and a record can be made useless without being made wrong. Nothing in the transcript is false; it is only unreadable, and unreadable is enough.
example: *"Six hours of **depositioning** produced four hundred pages, and the only complete answer in them was the witness's name."*
